One night, Bun-Bun the bunny looked up at the sky. The moon was round and yellow, like a big crunchy carrot!
"I want to taste the moon carrot!" said Bun-Bun. He hopped, and hopped, and hopped, but the moon was much too high.
Princess Luna smiled. "The moon is not a carrot, silly bunny. It's a night light for everyone!"
Then Luna gave Bun-Bun a real carrot from the garden. Crunch, crunch! It was the yummiest carrot ever.
Bun-Bun yawned a big bunny yawn, curled up in his cozy bed, and said good night to the moon. The end.
Pip the little kitten could not sleep. She looked out of the window and saw a tiny twinkling star.
"Star light, star bright, I wish I could fly tonight!" whispered Pip.
Whoosh! Stardust the unicorn flew by the window. "Hop on, Pip!" Together they flew over the castle and the sparkly sea.
They waved hello to the moon and the stars, and the stars twinkled back.
Then Stardust brought Pip home to her mommy, Mimi. Pip snuggled up and dreamed happy dreams. The end.
Dot the baby dragon had little wings, but he did not know how to fly.
He flapped and flapped. Bump! He landed in the flowers. "Oh no," said Dot.
"Try again!" said Princess Luna. "Everybody needs to practice."
Dot flapped one more time, and up, up, up he went, all the way over the apple tree!
"I did it!" cheered Dot. That night he fell asleep with a big smile, dreaming of flying. The end.
Shelly the sea turtle loved to sing to her babies at night.
"Swish, swish, says the sea. Sleep, sleep, little ones, close to me."
The fish came to listen. The starfish came to listen. Even Marina the mermaid came to listen.
The moon made a silver path on the water, and the waves rocked everyone gently.
Soon all the little turtles were fast asleep. Good night, sea. Good night, Shelly. The end.
On Snowy Hill, Pingo the penguin was getting ready for bed.
"Brrr, I'm a little cold," said Pingo. So the snowflakes came down softly, softly.
They made a white, fluffy blanket over the hill, the trees and the igloo.
Pingo snuggled into his warm igloo with his three little brothers, all in a row.
"Good night, snowflakes," said Pingo. And the snowflakes whispered, "Good night, Pingo." The end.
